atoms.sound: I am going to Lille, in France! My parents are driving us to Dover, but we are leaving our car there. Instead, we are crossing the English Channel on a type of boat called a ferry. Then, we can catch a train to Lille on the other side!

atoms.a: Where is Mohammed going on holiday?
How is he getting to France?
What transport are they going to use in France?

atoms.sound: Attention all passengers. We are sorry to announce that the ferry service to Calais is currently delayed due to technical problems. Please note that passengers travelling without a vehicle may already begin to board.

b.sound: The boat to Calais will not leave on time.
The boat to Calais will leave on time.
Mohammed and his family can board immediately.
Mohammed’s family has to wait to board.

atoms.a: Which train is Mohammed going to take?
b: Mohammed will take the train at 14:40.

atoms.a: How often do the trains to Paris run?
b: ++The trains to Paris run every hour.
The trains to Paris run every twenty minutes.
The trains to Paris run once a day.
++The train to Dunkerque is not running.
The train to Lille is not running.
The train to Paris is not running.

atoms.a: Mohammed’s ticket is for one adult passenger.
Mohammed is sitting in Coach B.
Mohammed does not have a seat reservation.

atoms.sound: We have lots of fun plans for Lille! We will walk to the market on the first day before renting bikes to ride around the city — apparently it’s really nice to cycle by the river! There is also a bus service we can take to travel to the nature park nearby!

atoms.a: In which two ways do Mohammed and his family plan to get around Lille?
b: ++They plan to travel on a bus.
They plan to travel on a train.

atoms.a: Where does Mohammed want to cycle in Lille?
b: ++He wants to cycle along the river.
He wants to cycle to the market.
He wants to cycle around the nature park.

atoms.a: Where does the bus service go to?
b: ++The bus service goes to the nature park.
The bus service goes to the river.
The bus service goes to the market.
